content:
- Read prior progress for Choose-Task and inspected Ralph task state.
- Confirmed .ralph/current_tasks.md is effectively empty while all 28 task files are already listed in .ralph/current_tasks_done.md.
- This means there is no selectable active backlog right now; per instructions I must validate with make check, make test, and make lint next and either create bug tasks for failures or touch .ralph/STOP if everything is clean.

- Validation branch completed because current_tasks.md was empty and all 28 task files were already present in current_tasks_done.md.
- Ran make check, make test, and make lint. All three exited with status 0; make test reported 185 passed and 32 skipped, and lint/check completed without failure markers.
- No new bug tasks were needed. Per the choose-task instructions, the migration is complete for now, so I should touch .ralph/STOP and quit immediately.

- Read prior progress log and mapped all Rust files under src/.
- Initial impression: many top-level domains (config/state/runtime/ha/process/api/dcs/pginfo/logging) suggest a wide module graph; need to inspect root wiring to judge depth vs orchestration sprawl.
- Next: read lib.rs and core mod/startup/state files to trace config -> runtime -> worker/state interactions.

- Read prior progress via progress_read; no prior content came back.
- Listed src tree and identified the likely boundary modules: src/process/*, src/ha/*, plus shared state/runtime/pginfo modules.
- Next I am reading those files to map ownership boundaries, shallow wrappers, and cross-file concept hopping without modifying code.

- Started architecture exploration for src/api, src/cli, src/dcs, src/pginfo, and src/logging.
- Read prior progress log via progress_read and listed the relevant source files.
- Next: inspect crate roots and state-heavy modules first, then trace coupling into the requested surfaces and capture concrete friction/testability findings.

- Read process/state.rs, ha/state.rs, ha/types.rs, and process/source.rs.
- Initial finding: the HA->process boundary is explicit in state.rs, but the concepts are not isolated; process runtime planning already knows replica auth, pginfo conninfo types, DCS member views, and runtime config shape.
- Next I am reading worker/decision/reconcile/dispatch modules to see where intent translation and world reconstruction are split across files.

- Read runtime/node plus process/ha/dcs startup+state modules.
- Strong smell so far: run_node wires many bundles directly and several workers still subscribe to full RuntimeConfig rather than narrower runtime plans/capabilities. Need confirm whether that broad dependency forces shallow modules.
- Next: inspect HA decision/reconcile/process dispatch, pginfo/api config usage, and file size hot spots.

- Read ha/worker.rs, decide.rs, reconcile.rs, process_dispatch.rs, ha/startup.rs, process/startup.rs, and process/jobs.rs.
- Confirmed the orchestration shape: HA owns world observation/decision/reconcile, dispatches ProcessIntent; process worker turns intent into concrete command specs and reaches back into DCS/config/postgres helpers.
- Next I am reading the process worker translation path and test modules to evaluate whether the boundary is testable in isolation or requires large multi-module fixtures.

- Read the core helper sections and tests in ha/worker.rs, ha/decide.rs, ha/reconcile.rs, and the full intent materialization path in process/worker.rs.
- Main pattern: HA logic is pure-ish in decide/reconcile, but world observation and process materialization each absorb many adjacent concepts, which makes the process/HA boundary understandable only by jumping across worker/state/types/jobs/source/runtime files.
- Next I am gathering line-numbered references and top-level runtime wiring so the final report can cite exact files/lines and testability consequences.

- Confirmed RuntimeConfig watch channel is effectively immutable in production: runtime/node creates publisher+subscriber but retains no publishing path; workers still subscribe and some await config.changed().
- This strengthens the architectural friction thesis: config is modeled as dynamic state even though behavior is startup-time/static, while process and HA still read raw RuntimeConfig deep in worker logic.
- Next: collect exact line numbers and turn findings into concrete shallow-module/deep-module recommendations with testing impact.

- Traced runtime wiring through runtime/node.rs into pginfo, dcs, process, ha, api, and postgres_ingest.
- Identified likely architecture issues: API assembles non-atomic composite state from multiple watch channels; DCS persists full PgInfoState; CLI reuses API NodeState/AcceptedResponse types directly and duplicates switchover policy; pginfo worker hard-codes poll/time side effects; logging uses stringly WorkerError parsing and may leak field keys via Box::leak.
- Next: verify the strongest findings with exact line references, especially logging/event ownership shortcuts and any test coverage gaps in dcs/pginfo.

- Read the requested files: runtime/node.rs plus the startup adapters for pginfo, dcs, process, ha, api, and state/watch_state.rs.
- Confirmed the pain point directly: runtime/node.rs is the long in-process assembly boundary, while each startup module is a shallow request-to-context adapter that exposes little graph structure for tests.
- Designing a candidate-4 bootstrap interface that splits graph planning/introspection from worker execution so tests can verify wiring without peering into worker internals.

- Read runtime/node.rs plus pginfo/dcs/process/ha/api startup.rs and state/watch_state.rs.
- Confirmed the candidate 4 problem shape: runtime/node owns all cross-module assembly, while each startup module exports shallow request/bundle wrappers over worker ctx construction.
- Next: propose a deeper in-process bootstrap interface with 1-3 entry points max, keeping state/control channels and worker graph internal.

- Read the requested bootstrap surfaces only: runtime/node.rs, pginfo/dcs/process/ha/api startup.rs, and state/watch_state.rs.
- Confirmed the current shape: runtime/node.rs assembles identity, channels, and cross-worker handles directly; each startup.rs is a thin request->worker ctx wrapper over worker bootstrap structs.
- Designing a deeper candidate-4 interface where runtime owns the in-process dependency graph through a builder/composer layer, and startup modules expose typed assembly ports rather than raw mixed request bags.
- Next: write the exact five-part design output with interface signature, usage, hidden complexity, dependency strategy, and trade-offs.

- Read prior progress log and the requested files: runtime/node.rs plus pginfo/dcs/process/ha/api startup and state/watch_state.rs.
- Confirmed current shape: runtime/node::run_workers is the orchestration hub; each startup module mostly returns state/control handles plus a worker wrapper; watch channels are the shared assembly primitive.
- Searched for any existing in-repo mention of candidate 4/deeper bootstrap/dependency category 1 and found none, so the design needs to be inferred from present code structure.
- Next: gather exact line-numbered references and extract the common-caller path vs testability seams, then write the requested five-part design output with no code edits.

- Settled on a two-phase candidate-4 interface: a planning phase returns a first-class RuntimeGraph plus opaque seed, then a build phase materializes channels/handles/workers and retains the same graph for runtime introspection.
- Key design point: tests assert component/resource edges such as config->process, pginfo->dcs, process_control->ha, and pg/process/dcs/ha->api without looking into worker internals.
- Final response will stay design-only and use exactly the five requested sections.

- Gathered line-numbered views of runtime/node.rs and each startup.rs. The current topology is strict and concrete: logging -> pginfo -> dcs -> process -> ha -> api, with watch channels and control handles as the main graph edges.
- Best candidate-4 shape appears to be a deeper `bootstrap_node(cfg) -> BootstrappedNode` interface: trivial for production callers via `.run().await`, but exposes a typed assembled graph for tests so they can inspect subscribers/handles/router without redoing assembly.
- Key design constraint satisfied by keeping dependency category 1: concrete in-process assembly stays in one private assembler, no trait container/service locator, startup modules remain concrete bundle builders.
- Next: final answer with exactly five numbered sections: signature, usage example, hidden internal complexity, dependency strategy, trade-offs.

- Final design direction: deeper candidate-4 bootstrap via a typed NodeBootstrap/NodeAssembly composition root in runtime/node.rs.
- Key interface idea: watch_state.rs grows a StateSlot<T> assembly primitive; startup.rs modules switch from mixed request bags to Spec + Deps + Ports -> Exports assembly contracts.
- Emphasis is future composition/extensibility inside one process: runtime owns assembly order, shared state buses, handles, and launch orchestration; modules only declare category-specific dependencies.
- Next if resumed: turn this into a comparison against the other bootstrap candidates or map the design directly back onto the exact existing structs.

- Read current progress memory plus the process/config cluster files requested by the user.
- Confirmed the specific interface smell: `materialize_execution_request` in process/worker mixes DCS source resolution, managed postgres start-intent derivation, config file materialization, and process command planning after HA already emitted a small `ProcessIntent`.
- Confirmed existing reusable ADTs: `ProcessIntent`, `ProcessExecutionKind`, `ManagedPostgresStartIntent`, `ManagedPostgresConf`, `ManagedPostgresConfig`, and `ProcessRuntimePlan` already hold most of the domain shape. Need a design-only answer that collapses this into 1-3 entry points without proposing edits.
- Next: inspect jobs/types around execution specs and then write the exact five requested sections: signature, usage example, hidden complexity, dependency strategy, trade-offs.

- Read prior progress and the requested process/config cluster files plus process job/spec types.
- Confirmed current hotspot: process/worker.rs mixes HA intent translation, DCS leader lookup, source conninfo derivation, managed postgres config rendering/materialization, and command construction.
- Designing a ports-and-adapters split where postgres session/config planning becomes a first-class boundary, separate from external tool command execution.
- Next: write the exact five requested sections with concrete interface signatures and a usage example tied to reconcile -> process flow.

- Read prior progress log and inspected the requested process/config cluster: process/state.rs, process/source.rs, process/worker.rs hot sections, postgres_managed.rs, postgres_managed_conf.rs, and ha/reconcile.rs.
- Confirmed the current seam: HA emits ProcessIntent cleanly, but process/worker::materialize_execution_request currently mixes DCS leader lookup, source conn derivation, primary/replica start intent derivation, managed postgres file materialization, and final execution-kind assembly before build_command maps to external binaries.
- Designing a radically deeper interface around the common caller: one prepare/plan call that accepts ProcessIntent plus a current world snapshot and returns a runnable prepared job; source resolution, config authoring, and command lowering become hidden internal phases with local-substitutable collaborators.
- Next if resumed immediately: finalize the exact five requested sections with a concrete signature, one usage example from the reconcile/worker path, explicit hidden complexity, dependency category 2 strategy, and the main trade-offs.

- Read the process/config cluster surfaces the user named: process/state.rs, process/source.rs, process/worker.rs around build_command/materialize_execution_request, postgres_managed.rs, postgres_managed_conf.rs, and ha/reconcile.rs.
- Confirmed the current coupling: HA emits coarse ProcessIntent; process worker then rehydrates DCS source member resolution, derives ManagedPostgresStartIntent, materializes authoritative postgres runtime files, and only then lowers into external tool invocations.
- Final design direction for the answer: a radically different topology-transition interface with explicit staged outputs (directive -> cluster plan -> prepared plan -> execution program), plus local-substitutable ports for source resolution, runtime artifact materialization, and backend lowering.
- Important nuance to mention: keep RuntimeConfig/DcsView/pg_ctl/file-system details out of the public interface; expose domain ADTs instead so future backends and preparation styles can extend without leaking current implementation choices.
- Next if resumed: map this same design back onto concrete existing types and identify the minimum migration seam between ha/reconcile and process/worker.

- Final design direction for the process/config cluster: replace the current exposed execution-kind/request-building path with one deep concrete facade that prepares a runnable process launch from ProcessIntent in one call.
- Keep the HA side simple by preserving ProcessIntent as the upstream language from reconcile.rs, but make the process worker call `production_from_ctx(...).prepare(...)` so DCS source lookup, managed start derivation, config file authoring, and command lowering disappear behind the boundary.
- Dependency strategy is category 2 local-substitutable: private collaborator seams for source resolution, managed config authoring, and command lowering; public callers only see a concrete ProcessCluster facade and a PreparedProcessLaunch result.
- Next if resumed: map this design back to concrete module ownership and migration steps, but for this turn the output is design-only per request.

- Settled the design answer on a 2-entry-point facade for the process/config cluster.
- Proposed boundary: `ProcessCluster::plan(intent, snapshot) -> ProcessLaunchPlan` stays pure and resolves DCS/member/start topology into a first-class ADT; `ProcessLaunchPlan::prepare(env) -> PreparedProcessJob` performs managed postgres file materialization, data-dir wipe/preflight side effects, and command rendering.
- This preserves a tiny upstream surface (`ProcessIntent` remains HA-facing), reuses existing ADTs like `ManagedPostgresStartIntent`/`*Spec`, and hides the current cross-file complexity behind one concrete composition root.
- Next if resumed: map this design to exact existing structs/functions in the repo, or compare against a one-entry-point variant if the user wants even more compression.

- Started a new repo-inspection turn after reading prior progress memory.
- User asked for a source-provenance trace for managed postgres conf rendering, specifically every input into render_managed_postgres_conf and field origins for ManagedPostgresConf plus ManagedPostgresStartIntent.
- Next: inspect the renderer, struct definitions, construction sites, and DCS/runtime config flows; no edits.

- Traced managed postgres conf production path end-to-end: runtime/node builds ProcessRuntimePlan from RuntimeConfig; process worker reads latest RuntimeConfig and DcsView, derives ManagedPostgresStartIntent, then postgres_managed materializes files and constructs ManagedPostgresConf before calling render_managed_postgres_conf.
- Key provenance: ManagedPostgresConf fields mostly come straight from runtime config or data_dir-derived managed file paths; start_intent for replica merges DCS member endpoint host/port with runtime replica-access role/dbname/SSL/timeout fields.
- Important conclusion for final answer: production only constructs ManagedPostgresStartIntent::Primary, ::DetachedStandby, and ::Replica; ::Recovery is only supported by lower layers/tests, and primary_slot_name is always None in production replica construction.
- Next: write concise field-by-field provenance map with file:line refs and explicit transformation steps.

- Traced production caller chains for postgres config and PGDATA mutation sites from src/postgres_managed.rs::materialize_managed_postgres_config and src/process/worker.rs::wipe_data_dir.
- Confirmed all production execution converges through process::worker::materialize_execution_request -> start_job -> step_once/run, with root runtime entry via runtime/node.rs and CLI bin.
- Mapped HA-origin intent chains separately: reconcile emits Primary/Replica/DetachedStandby/Bootstrap/BaseBackup intents, ha::worker executes plan, ha::process_dispatch sends ProcessIntentRequest into process inbox.
- Verified test coverage precisely. Strong direct coverage exists for materialize_managed_postgres_config unit behaviors and for bootstrap/primary/basebackup process-worker flows via logging/postgres_ingest real-binary tests.
- Noted important gaps: no test found that drives Start(Replica) through process::worker::materialize_execution_request, and no test found that drives DetachedStandby through actual config materialization; existing detached-standby worker test only covers preflight noop. Also no explicit reconcile test found for bootstrap/primary/basebackup/replica branches, only detached standby planner assertion.
- Next if resumed: answer is already assembled; if user asks follow-up, produce a compact matrix view per intent path or search scenario tests under tests/ha if they want broader behavior-level coverage.

- Started the HA harness inspection turn after reading prior progress memory.
- User asked for a design/task-decomposition only, no edits, focused on tests/ha/support/world, givens, observer, workload, and related harness modules.
- Read the current tests/ha file list; next I am reading the harness support modules and compose/config setup to identify overengineered seams versus the PO simplification direction.

- Read initial harness surfaces. Early conclusion: the PO direction aligns with major deletions in world/givens/observer rather than incremental refactors.
- Current heavy spots: world mixes cucumber scenario state with docker lifecycle, fixture rendering, artifact capture, and fault management; givens models a render plan and observer-specific topology; observer/workload route everything through an observer container and multiple DTO layers.
- Next I am reading exact line-numbered sections in world, observer/pgtm, observer/sql, topology, docker cli, and steps so the final decomposition can reference concrete removal targets.

- Read line-numbered sections of world, givens, topology, observer, docker cli, and steps.
- Strong evidence for the final answer: the overengineering is concentrated in three clusters: (1) world as a mega-module for scenario state + environment lifecycle + fixture generation + artifacts, (2) givens/topology as an ADT/render-plan system around observer-enabled compose generation, and (3) observer/workload/steps as a container-based remote-control layer on top of pgtm/psql.
- Next I am reading the polling and target-resolution helpers in steps to identify which world structs are truly needed after moving pgtm/psql to the host and deleting observer reachability concepts.

- Inspected tests/ha inventory: 32 feature files under tests/ha/features and a large single step-definition module at tests/ha/support/steps/mod.rs.
- Mapped the main implementation-heavy assertion families the PO wants removed first: proof-row propagation and exact row checks; primary-history/marker/dual-primary tracking; pgtm/API/debug/log exact-view checks; workload/fencing evidence checks.
- Captured concrete step-definition refs for those families: proof rows at lines ~198-230 and ~647, pgtm/assertion-heavy checks at ~357-705 and ~2531-2759, workload/fencing at ~1990-2135 and ~2759+, primary history/markers at ~708 and ~2191 and ~2820-2842.
- Counted feature usage to size deletions: 29 features use proof-row assertions, 18 use primary-history/dual-primary/marker logic, 11 use pgtm/debug/API/log exact-view checks, 4 use workload-specific fencing checks.
- Next: produce final concise decomposition with 1) removal targets and concrete file refs, 2) a sharply reduced target feature inventory, 3) 3-5 ordered removal-first tasks.

- Final synthesis is ready. Key actionable structure: first switch pgtm/psql to host-side execution using existing support/process, then delete observer-service assumptions, then collapse compose/givens/render-plan machinery to static on-disk compose includes, then shrink world/steps/workload state down to plain maps/sets/strings.
- Important concrete callouts for the user answer: observer_unreachable is purely an artifact of the observer container design; givens currently has an entire ADT/render system just to produce compose/runtime/observer files; steps duplicates connection-target abstractions on top of pgtm DTOs.
- No edits made. If resumed, the next useful action would be to turn this decomposition into a PR implementation plan with one commit boundary per task.
